what_it_does: FPGAs (Field-Programmable Gate Arrays) are chips whose internal circuits can be rewired in software, making them attractive for renting out in a data center to many different users. Sharing an FPGA among tenants requires reprogramming sections of it on demand — a process called partial reconfiguration — but when multiple tenants want to reconfigure at the same time, they compete for the reprogramming hardware, blocking each other and slowing everyone down. VersaSlot addresses this by dividing the FPGA into a mix of 'big' and 'little' programming slots: large tasks that take a long time get big slots so they are not blocked by frequent small reconfigurations, while short tasks use the small slots and turn over quickly. The system also supports live migration — moving a running task from one physical FPGA board to another across a cluster — so the overall scheduling can be balanced without interrupting work.
